drafts.subject: Re: Prospective GSoC contributor - where to start?
drafts.message:
Hi Fatima,

Thanks so much for reaching out and for your interest in contributing to Jaseci! It's great to hear you're comfortable with Python and have already started exploring Jac—that's definitely a solid foundation for working with our codebase.

For getting started, I recommend checking out our core Jaseci repository where we have a number of beginner-friendly issues labeled as "good-first-issue." These are specifically chosen to help new contributors get familiar with the project structure and development workflow. You can find these issues here: https://github.com/jaseci/jaseci/labels/good-first-issue

Additionally, if you want to dive deeper into Jac, the jac-lang repository has some interesting tasks and enhancements that are beginner-appropriate. Your Python skills will come in handy, especially since a lot of our tooling and extensions integrate closely with Python.

Please feel free to ask if you want any help picking an issue or need guidance on setting up your environment. We're excited to have you onboard and look forward to your contributions!

Best,
Impact (on behalf of the Jaseci team)

drafts.subject: Re: Bug: edge traversal returns duplicates after node delete (repro attached)
drafts.message:
Hi Omar,

Thank you for bringing this to our attention with such a clear repro. The behavior you're describing with Jac 0.10.2—where deleting a node results in duplicate edges during traversal—is not a widely documented issue, so this may be a regression or edge case we need to investigate further.

We appreciate your offer to file a GitHub issue; that would be very helpful for tracking and resolving the problem. If you could share the full code snippet and any additional context, it will aid our debugging process.

For a potential workaround in the meantime, you might consider explicitly cleaning up edges connected to a node before its deletion, ensuring no stale references remain that could cause duplicates during traversal. This manual edge pruning may help mitigate the issue until we can implement a fix.

We'll prioritize looking into this and update you as soon as we have more information.

Best regards,
Impact Team

drafts.subject: Re: Press: quote on agentic programming languages (deadline Aug 5 EOD)
drafts.message:
Hi Grace,

Thank you for reaching out. General-purpose programming languages often fall short for agentic software because they lack built-in abstractions and constructs tailored for autonomous decision-making and interaction within dynamic environments. Agent-native languages provide specialized frameworks that enable more efficient modeling of agent behaviors, communication, and adaptability, which are crucial for developing sophisticated, goal-driven agents.

Please let me know if you need any further information.

Best regards,
Impact
Jaseci Team
